title: ScaffoldSwap: Are Discrete Speech Units Necessary as a Temporal Scaffold for Audio-Driven 3D Facial Animation?

contributions.purpose: Isolate the effect of speech representation on 3D facial animation quality by controlled comparison.
contributions.mechanism: ScaffoldSwap ablation comparing three speech conditioning approaches under an identical TCN decoder, training procedure, and prosody features: (A) continuous SSL features (WavLM-base-plus), (B) discrete speech units (HuBERT-base + k-means, K=200), (C) phoneme+timing from Montreal Forced Aligner.
contributions.evaluation: First systematic comparison, evaluated on BIWI and VOCASET by Lip Vertex Error (LVE), 3 seeds; both structured scaffolds beat SSL by 5-10%.
contributions.source_quote: The first systematic comparison of speech conditioning approaches (SSL, discrete units, phoneme+timing) for audio-driven 3D facial animation under controlled experimental conditions.

contributions.purpose: Determine whether discretization itself (not the underlying representation) drives gains.
contributions.mechanism: Ablation comparing discrete units (HuBERT + k-means) against HuBERT-continuous (same encoder without k-means quantization).
contributions.evaluation: HuBERT-continuous LVE 9.494e-6 is 17.5% worse than discrete units 8.080e-6 on BIWI; discrete units also beat phoneme+timing by 0.5-1.3% (gap exceeds 1 std by 5.2-7.1x), rejecting the scaffold-equivalence hypothesis.
contributions.domain: Discrete speech tokenization / information bottleneck analysis
contributions.source_quote: Evidence that discretization provides a beneficial information bottleneck: k-means quantization of HuBERT features improves LVE by 17.5% over continuous features.

contributions.purpose: Assess whether explicit timing features add value beyond frame-level phoneme identity.
contributions.mechanism: Ablate within-phoneme position and duration features from the phoneme+timing condition (Condition C).
contributions.evaluation: Removing timing features changes LVE by only +0.01% (8.188 -> 8.189e-6 on BIWI), indicating frame-level phoneme identity alone suffices; temporal-shuffle sanity check degrades LVE by 14.9%.
contributions.source_quote: The finding that explicit timing features (within-phoneme position and duration) are redundant-frame-level phoneme identity alone captures sufficient temporal structure.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Following the temporal scaffold approach proposed by Ex-Omni (Zhang et al., 2026), we extract features from HuBERT-base-ls960 (Hsu et al., 2021) and quantize them to K = 200 discrete unit IDs via k-means clustering.

A recent development in this space is the use of discrete speech units as temporal scaffolds for facial animation. Ex-Omni (Zhang et al., 2026) proposes quantizing self-supervised speech features into discrete tokens... it remains unclear whether discretization is uniquely beneficial, or whether simpler phoneme+timing scaffolds derived from forced alignment can provide equivalent temporal structure.
Following prior work (Fan et al., 2021; Cudeiro et al., 2019), we compress the high-dimensional vertex space using PCA, predicting 512-dimensional coefficients.

notes: The discrete-vs-phoneme+timing gap is modest (0.5-1.3%); authors note phoneme+timing offers a viable lightweight alternative achieving ~90% of the improvement over SSL. Datasets are small (BIWI 0.33h, VOCASET 0.56h).
